nodes.summary: For literals $l = (x, p)$ and $l' = (x', q)$, each a variable $x, x' \in \mathbb{N}$ with a polarity $p, q \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, the adjacency bit of $l$ and $l'$ is false when they are complementary, that is $x = x'$ and $p \ne q$, and true otherwise. It is the adjacency of two occurrences in different clauses in Karp's graph.
nodes.title: Karp adjacency of two literals

nodes.summary: Call two literal occurrences (clause index, variable, polarity) adjacent when they lie in different clauses and are not complementary. Let $f$ be a map on occurrences such that $f(a)$ and $f(b)$ are adjacent exactly when $a$ and $b$ are, for all occurrences $a$ and $b$. Then for every list of occurrences $o_1, \dots, o_k$, the row-by-row pair bits of $f(o_1), \dots, f(o_k)$ equal those of $o_1, \dots, o_k$.
nodes.title: Row-by-row pair bits see only adjacency

nodes.summary: For a list of literal occurrences (clause index, variable, polarity), the row-by-row pair bits are defined recursively: the empty list has none, and for a list $o, o_1, \dots, o_k$ they are the adjacency bits of $o$ with $o_k, \dots, o_1$, in that order, followed by the row-by-row pair bits of $o_1, \dots, o_k$. Two occurrences are adjacent when they lie in different clauses and are not complementary.

If $V$ is empty, it moves to the accept label if the input stack $X$ is empty and to the reject label otherwise. If $V$ is not empty, it pops the top symbol of $V$, reads it as a bit $z$ (a non-bit symbol reads as false), and continues with the rest of the walk step for $m$, $c$ and $z$.

Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
